title: Experimental Design
subject: Statistics

cards.prompt: Distinguish sampling, assignment, observation, and analysis units in an experiment. Why can counting measurement rows overstate replication?
cards.definition: A unit-role map identifies what is sampled, what receives an assigned treatment, what is measured, and what level is analyzed. These roles can coincide or be nested. For example, a school study may sample schools, assign teaching methods to classrooms, and measure individual students. Students in the same assigned classroom are not automatically independent treatment replications; the analysis must respect the assignment and dependence structure.
required_concepts: Identify sampling, treatment-assignment, observation, and analysis roles, allowing different or nested units.
The number of measurements need not equal the number of independent replications; account for clustering and the assignment level.
accepted_variants: Sampling might select schools, assignment randomize teaching methods to classrooms, observation record individual students, and analysis model student outcomes with classroom clustering. These distinct, nested unit roles show why more student measurements do not automatically provide more independent treatment replications.
major_error_concepts: Treating every measurement row as an independent treatment replicate regardless of shared experimental units or assignment.

cards.prompt: What is the analysis unit, and how must an analysis handle observations nested within shared experimental units?
cards.definition: The analysis unit is the entity or level represented in the statistical analysis, such as a person, classroom, or plot. It need not equal the assignment unit, and its observations need not be independent. If student outcomes are analyzed after classroom-level assignment, the model or design-based uncertainty calculation must account for the shared assignment and relevant within-class dependence.
required_concepts: Identify the entity or level analyzed, distinguishing it from assignment and observation units where they differ.
Using individual rows does not establish independence; handle the relevant clustering or dependence in inference.
accepted_variants: Students can be the analysis units even when classrooms receive treatments, but their uncertainty calculation must respect classroom assignment and within-class dependence rather than treating every student as an independent experiment.
major_error_concepts: Analyzing student rows as independent treatment replications while ignoring their shared classroom assignment and correlated outcomes.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Confirmatory versus exploratory status.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between a prespecified decision test with calibrated error guarantees and a result-generating analysis needing new confirmation.
required_concepts: Confirmatory status requires a decision question and analysis declared before inspecting the result.
A confirmatory analysis uses the prespecified procedure to retain its calibrated error guarantees.
Exploratory status applies when the observed results generate or materially select the question or analysis.
An exploratory result needs transparent labeling and new confirmation rather than a backdated confirmatory story.
major_error_concepts: Backdating the slice rationale and reporting it as confirmatory.

cards.prompt: Define Control condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The counterfactual reference condition frozen with the same detail as treatment except for declared differences.
required_concepts: The counterfactual reference condition frozen with the same detail as treatment except for declared differences.
major_error_concepts: Using historical runs with different tasks compute and logging as the control.

cards.prompt: Define Ethics and governance boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The rule that statistical validity does not supply consent fairness policy safety approval or deployment authority.
required_concepts: The rule that statistical validity does not supply consent fairness policy safety approval or deployment authority.
major_error_concepts: Treating random assignment as ethical authorization.

cards.prompt: Define Experimental estimand. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The precise treatment-effect summary over declared units conditions outcomes and assignment or exposure regime.
required_concepts: The precise treatment-effect summary over declared units conditions outcomes and assignment or exposure regime.
major_error_concepts: Reporting a p-value without stating what effect quantity it concerns.

cards.prompt: Define Experimental unit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The smallest unit that can receive a treatment condition independently under the physical protocol.
required_concepts: The smallest unit that can receive a treatment condition independently under the physical protocol.
major_error_concepts: Calling each event an experimental unit because it has one row.

cards.prompt: Define Exposure unit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The unit whose received treatment or spillover exposure must be represented to define its potential outcome.
required_concepts: The unit whose received treatment or spillover exposure must be represented to define its potential outcome.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the randomization label alone describes actual exposure under spillovers.

cards.prompt: Define Guardrail outcome. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A prespecified harm or constraint metric that can block a favorable primary-result decision.
required_concepts: A prespecified harm or constraint metric that can block a favorable primary-result decision.
major_error_concepts: Treating every measured diagnostic as another interchangeable primary outcome.

cards.prompt: What makes experimental replications independent, and why are repeated measurements on one unit not automatically independent replications?
cards.definition: Independent replications repeat the relevant experiment using independently generated units or runs under the stated conditions and dependence assumptions. Merely taking another measurement of one unit is technical repetition, not another independent experimental unit. Independence must be justified for the relevant variation; different row labels or repeated execution alone do not establish it.
required_concepts: Replication uses distinct experimental units or runs with justified independence for the relevant variation.
Repeated measurements of one unit do not automatically create independent experimental replications.
accepted_variants: Several separately grown plants can provide independent growth replications under a justified design. Measuring one plant repeatedly improves measurement information but does not turn that plant into several independent growth experiments.
major_error_concepts: Counting repeated measurements of the same plant as independent plant-growth replications without addressing their common unit and dependence.

cards.prompt: Define Observation unit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The unit at which one measurement row is recorded without implying independence or assignment.
required_concepts: The unit at which one measurement row is recorded without implying independence or assignment.
major_error_concepts: Equating row count with independent replication.

cards.prompt: Define Primary outcome. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The prespecified response that anchors the main decision and error guarantee.
required_concepts: The prespecified response that anchors the main decision and error guarantee.
major_error_concepts: Choosing the most favorable metric after seeing results.

cards.prompt: Define Protocol freeze. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The timestamped commitment to eligibility treatments outcomes assignments exclusions analysis stopping and decisions before protected outcomes are inspected.
required_concepts: The timestamped commitment to eligibility treatments outcomes assignments exclusions analysis stopping and decisions before protected outcomes are inspected.
major_error_concepts: Calling a mutable notebook a protocol when choices can change silently.

cards.prompt: Define Randomization unit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The unit whose treatment label is generated by the assignment mechanism.
required_concepts: The unit whose treatment label is generated by the assignment mechanism.
major_error_concepts: Using session count as the assignment denominator when labels persist by user.

cards.prompt: Define Research question. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A manipulable and answerable contrast connecting an intervention to a declared response in a declared target and time window.
required_concepts: A manipulable and answerable contrast connecting an intervention to a declared response in a declared target and time window.
major_error_concepts: Leaving better undefined or asking a causal question without an intervention.

cards.prompt: Define Experimental response measurement rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The measured outcome rule including unit scale direction timing aggregation and missingness handling.
required_concepts: The measured outcome rule including unit scale direction timing aggregation and missingness handling.
major_error_concepts: Using a subjective good outcome whose evaluator and time window are unstated.

cards.prompt: Define Sampling unit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: A sampling unit is an entity or group eligible for selection at a specified stage of the sampling design. For example, a two-stage survey may first sample schools and then students within selected schools. Sampling units can differ from treatment-assignment, observation, and analysis units. The definition concerns the selection mechanism, not a universal rule that all sampling precedes treatment assignment.
required_concepts: Identify the entity selected at the stated stage of the sampling mechanism.
Distinguish sampling from assignment or measurement roles; units may differ across stages.
accepted_variants: In a two-stage school survey, schools are first-stage sampling units and students are second-stage units. The sampling role is about selection and need not be the treatment-assignment or analysis role.
major_error_concepts: Calling repeated measurements on one sampled participant separately sampled population members solely because they produce several rows.

cards.prompt: Define Target population. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The units and conditions over which the final estimand is intended to generalize.
required_concepts: The units and conditions over which the final estimand is intended to generalize.
major_error_concepts: Generalizing from a convenience sample of university volunteers to every age group and setting without a justified generalization argument.

cards.prompt: Define Treatment condition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact intervention version dose timing delivery and co-interventions assigned under one protocol.
required_concepts: The exact intervention version dose timing delivery and co-interventions assigned under one protocol.
major_error_concepts: Naming only a fertilizer while allowing its dose, application timing, delivery, or accompanying treatments to differ without recording those differences.

cards.prompt: Define Allocation concealment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** prevention of foreknowledge of the next assignment by those enrolling or routing units so eligibility cannot be manipulated.
required_concepts: prevention of foreknowledge of the next assignment by those enrolling or routing units so eligibility cannot be manipulated.
major_error_concepts: Treating random sequence generation as sufficient when recruiters can see future labels.

cards.prompt: Define Allocation ratio. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The prespecified arm probability or fixed count controlling treatment exposure cost precision and feasible contrasts.
required_concepts: The prespecified arm probability or fixed count controlling treatment exposure cost precision and feasible contrasts.
major_error_concepts: Choosing the ratio from observed outcomes.

cards.prompt: Define Bernoulli randomization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** independent treatment assignment with declared probability for each unit and random realized treatment count.
required_concepts: independent treatment assignment with declared probability for each unit and random realized treatment count.
major_error_concepts: Conditioning after the fact on equal arm sizes without changing the reference design.

cards.prompt: Define Blinding boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Masking treatment identity from specified participants, operators, outcome assessors, or analysts where feasible to reduce behavior and measurement pathways without changing the assignment mechanism.
required_concepts: Blinding names which participants, operators, outcome assessors, or analysts are masked to treatment identity where feasible.
The masking reduces behavior and measurement pathways without changing the assignment mechanism.
major_error_concepts: Saying double blind without naming who is actually masked.

cards.prompt: Define Complete randomization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** uniform assignment among vectors with a fixed treatment count and therefore fixed realized arm sizes.
required_concepts: uniform assignment among vectors with a fixed treatment count and therefore fixed realized arm sizes.
major_error_concepts: Calling independent coin flips complete randomization despite variable arm sizes.

cards.prompt: Define Covariate balance in expectation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The randomization property that treatment and control covariate means agree over the assignment distribution not necessarily in one realized allocation.
required_concepts: The randomization property that treatment and control covariate means agree over the assignment distribution not necessarily in one realized allocation.
major_error_concepts: Claiming any observed imbalance proves randomization failed or that randomization guarantees equality.

cards.prompt: Define Crossover assignment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The randomized ordering of treatment sequences within units with period washout and carryover conditions declared.
required_concepts: The randomized ordering of treatment sequences within units with period washout and carryover conditions declared.
major_error_concepts: Using crossover when treatment has irreversible learning effects.

cards.prompt: Define Difference-in-means estimator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The treated sample mean minus control sample mean under the specified assignment and outcome units.
required_concepts: The treated sample mean minus control sample mean under the specified assignment and outcome units.
major_error_concepts: Using number of logged events rather than assigned units in the denominator.

cards.prompt: Define Finite-population average treatment effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The average over specified experimental units of Y_i(1)-Y_i(0) without requiring a superpopulation sampling claim.
required_concepts: The average over specified experimental units of Y_i(1)-Y_i(0) without requiring a superpopulation sampling claim.
major_error_concepts: Replacing the declared finite set with a broader population after seeing the answer.

cards.prompt: Define Fundamental causal missingness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The impossibility of observing the same unit under mutually exclusive treatment conditions at the same experimental time.
required_concepts: The impossibility of observing the same unit under mutually exclusive treatment conditions at the same experimental time.
major_error_concepts: Subtracting a different control unit and calling it the treated unit's individual effect.

cards.prompt: Define Matched-pair random assignment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** independent within-pair allocation of one unit to each treatment after pairs are fixed from pretreatment information.
required_concepts: independent within-pair allocation of one unit to each treatment after pairs are fixed from pretreatment information.
major_error_concepts: Randomizing all six units freely and analyzing as though pairs were enforced.

cards.prompt: Define Period and carryover effects. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** time-position and prior-treatment effects that can confound a naive within-unit treatment contrast in crossover designs.
required_concepts: time-position and prior-treatment effects that can confound a naive within-unit treatment contrast in crossover designs.
major_error_concepts: Attributing all within-unit improvement to the second treatment.

cards.prompt: Define Potential outcomes. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The indexed outcomes each unit would exhibit under each treatment or exposure condition in the specified design.
required_concepts: The indexed outcomes each unit would exhibit under each treatment or exposure condition in the specified design.
major_error_concepts: Treating the two potential outcomes as two repeated measurements available for one unit.

cards.prompt: Define Randomization distribution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The distribution of a declared statistic over allocations permitted by the actual assignment mechanism under an imputable null.
required_concepts: The distribution of a declared statistic over allocations permitted by the actual assignment mechanism under an imputable null.
major_error_concepts: Permuting individual observations when the design randomized matched pairs or clusters.

cards.prompt: Define a randomization-test p-value for a possibly nonuniform assignment mechanism.
cards.definition: Under an imputable null and the actual assignment law pi(z), a one-sided randomization p-value for larger T is sum_z pi(z) 1{T(z)≥T(z_obs)} over permitted assignments. It becomes the fraction of assignments at least as extreme only when those assignments are equiprobable. Freeze sidedness and ties; a Monte Carlo approximation needs its own valid sampling and finite-simulation convention rather than being called an exact enumeration.
required_concepts: Compute tail probability under the actual permitted-assignment law.
An unweighted proportion is valid for equiprobable assignments, not arbitrary probabilities.
Declare extremeness and tie rules before observing the result.
major_error_concepts: All permitted assignments count equally even if their randomization probabilities are unequal.

cards.prompt: Define sharpness of a randomization null and distinguish it from an average-effect null.
cards.definition: A sharp null specifies enough unit-level potential-outcome relations to impute every missing potential outcome needed for the randomization test from the observed data. The usual no-effect example is Y_i(1)=Y_i(0) for every i. In a binary-treatment no-interference design, a fully specified constant additive effect Y_i(1)=Y_i(0)+tau0 is also sharp. Merely asserting a zero average effect is not sharp.
required_concepts: Sharpness means the relevant missing potential outcomes can be imputed under the null.
Unitwise zero effect is an example, not the only sharp null.
An average-effect assertion alone does not determine individual missing outcomes.
major_error_concepts: A zero average treatment effect is sharp even if individual positive and negative effects cancel.

cards.prompt: Define Treatment fidelity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The check that assigned units received the intended condition at the intended version dose timing and isolation.
required_concepts: The check that assigned units received the intended condition at the intended version dose timing and isolation.
major_error_concepts: Silently dropping nonreceivers and calling the remaining comparison randomized.

cards.prompt: Define a balanced incomplete block design and state its two basic parameter identities.
cards.definition: A balanced incomplete block design with v treatments has b blocks, each containing k distinct treatments with k<v. Each treatment occurs in r blocks and each pair in lambda blocks. Double-counting gives vr=bk and lambda(v-1)=r(k-1). Equal block sizes alone do not establish treatment replication or pair balance; these parameter identities are necessary, not a general existence proof.
required_concepts: Declare treatment count v, block count b, block size k, replication r, and pair concurrence lambda.
Each treatment and pair have constant replication and concurrence.
State vr=bk and lambda(v-1)=r(k-1), with k<v.
major_error_concepts: Any b equally sized blocks form a BIBD regardless of which treatment pairs occur.

cards.prompt: Define Block degrees-of-freedom tradeoff. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The finite information cost of estimating or conditioning on many block levels when blocks do not predict response enough to compensate.
required_concepts: The finite information cost of estimating or conditioning on many block levels when blocks do not predict response enough to compensate.
major_error_concepts: Equating finer blocking with universally better design.

cards.prompt: Define Block effect and treatment contrast. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The separation of between-block level variation from within-block treatment comparison under an additive working structure.
required_concepts: The separation of between-block level variation from within-block treatment comparison under an additive working structure.
major_error_concepts: Comparing unweighted overall means when blocks have different treatment representation.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Blocked versus unblocked precision.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A blocked design compares treatments within groups formed from a predictive pretreatment variable and can remove block-related variation from residual error, whereas an unblocked design randomizes without those groups and avoids blocking restrictions and parameters. Blocking improves precision only when the removed variation outweighs its costs.
required_concepts: A blocked design compares treatments within groups formed from a predictive pretreatment variable and can remove block-related variation from residual error.
An unblocked design randomizes without those groups, avoiding blocking restrictions and parameters but leaving block-related variation in the residual error.
Blocking improves precision only when the pretreatment block variable is sufficiently predictive for the removed variation to outweigh the restrictions and added parameters.
major_error_concepts: Claiming balance alone proves a precision gain.

cards.prompt: Define Blocking principle. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** grouping similar experimental units before randomization and assigning treatments within groups to reduce irrelevant variation.
required_concepts: grouping similar experimental units before randomization and assigning treatments within groups to reduce irrelevant variation.
major_error_concepts: Blocking guarantees lower variance even when the block is unrelated or costs degrees of freedom.

cards.prompt: Define an incomplete block design and explain why its connectedness matters.
cards.definition: An incomplete block design has blocks that omit at least one treatment, commonly because each block has limited capacity. Its treatment-block incidence determines which contrasts are estimable. In the standard additive treatment/block model, a connected design permits all treatment contrasts; disconnected components prevent comparisons across components without additional assumptions.
required_concepts: Blocks need not contain every treatment.
Incidence and connectedness govern contrast estimability.
A disconnected incomplete design is possible, but it does not identify all between-treatment comparisons.
major_error_concepts: A disconnected treatment-block design is automatically a complete block design.

cards.prompt: Define Latin square additivity limit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The classical design limitation that treatment by row or column interactions are not separately estimable in one unreplicated square.
required_concepts: The classical design limitation that treatment by row or column interactions are not separately estimable in one unreplicated square.
major_error_concepts: Claiming two-way blocking controls every interaction.

cards.prompt: Define Latin square design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A treatment arrangement using rows and columns as two blocking directions so every treatment appears once per row and column.
required_concepts: A treatment arrangement using rows and columns as two blocking directions so every treatment appears once per row and column.
major_error_concepts: Using a fixed square without randomizing row column and treatment labels as required.

cards.prompt: Define Matched pairs as blocks. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The special two-treatment design where each pair is a block and one unit receives each treatment under randomized within-pair assignment.
required_concepts: The special two-treatment design where each pair is a block and one unit receives each treatment under randomized within-pair assignment.
major_error_concepts: Forming pairs after seeing outcomes.

cards.prompt: Define Nuisance factor. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A pretreatment source of variation not itself the primary scientific target but relevant to precision or assignment.
required_concepts: A pretreatment source of variation not itself the primary scientific target but relevant to precision or assignment.
major_error_concepts: Calling treatment-induced latency a nuisance covariate for blocking.

cards.prompt: Define Post-treatment blocking failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** conditioning or blocking on a variable changed by treatment which can alter the estimand and induce bias.
required_concepts: conditioning or blocking on a variable changed by treatment which can alter the estimand and induce bias.
major_error_concepts: Calling the resulting selected comparison a randomized subgroup effect.

cards.prompt: Define Pretreatment matching. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** forming pairs or blocks from information unaffected by assignment before randomization to improve comparability or precision.
required_concepts: forming pairs or blocks from information unaffected by assignment before randomization to improve comparability or precision.
major_error_concepts: Matching on a post-treatment variable or the outcome itself.

cards.prompt: Define Randomized complete block design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A design in which each block contains every treatment once or at the declared replication and allocation is randomized within blocks.
required_concepts: A design in which each block contains every treatment once or at the declared replication and allocation is randomized within blocks.
major_error_concepts: Calling a two-way observational table an RCBD without randomized treatment allocation.

cards.prompt: Define Restricted-randomization inference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement that analysis and null simulation honor every block pair balance or admissibility restriction imposed during assignment.
required_concepts: The requirement that analysis and null simulation honor every block pair balance or admissibility restriction imposed during assignment.
major_error_concepts: Analyzing as complete randomization after imposing restrictions.

cards.prompt: Define Treatment-by-block interaction boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** variation of treatment effects across blocks that makes a single additive effect insufficient and requires replication or a qualified weighted estimand.
required_concepts: variation of treatment effects across blocks that makes a single additive effect insufficient and requires replication or a qualified weighted estimand.
major_error_concepts: Deleting the interaction because blocks were nuisance factors.

cards.prompt: Distinguish true treatment replication from technical replication, including designs with constrained randomization.
cards.definition: True treatment replication uses distinct experimental units that receive the treatment under the declared randomization design. Technical replication repeats measurement or processing within the same experimental unit. Technical repeats can improve measurement precision but do not create new treatment-assignment units. Randomization labels need not be statistically independent: complete or blocked randomization can constrain labels while still supplying genuine unit replication.
required_concepts: Distinguish distinct treatment-assignment units from repeated measurements of one unit.
Technical repeats do not increase the number of independently informative treatment units by themselves.
Assignment constraints do not turn distinct experimental units into technical repeats.
major_error_concepts: Thirty measurements from one treated unit create thirty independently assigned treatment replicates.

cards.prompt: Define Within-block randomization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** assignment restricted inside each prespecified block so treatment comparisons use the correct randomization distribution.
required_concepts: assignment restricted inside each prespecified block so treatment comparisons use the correct randomization distribution.
major_error_concepts: Permuting labels across blocks and changing the design.

cards.prompt: Define Cell replication. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** independent experimental units assigned to the same treatment combination to estimate variation and permit lack-of-fit or interaction uncertainty.
required_concepts: independent experimental units assigned to the same treatment combination to estimate variation and permit lack-of-fit or interaction uncertainty.
major_error_concepts: Confusing repeated observations within a cell with independent cell replicates.

cards.term: Center points in a two-level design
cards.prompt: Define Center points in a two-level design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** replicated midpoint runs used to compare center response with corner average and detect aggregate curvature within the region.
required_concepts: replicated midpoint runs used to compare center response with corner average and detect aggregate curvature within the region.
major_error_concepts: Calling the center the global optimum.

cards.prompt: Distinguish Crossed versus nested factors.
cards.definition: **Definition.** crossed factors have every relevant level combination while nested levels occur only within one parent level.
required_concepts: Two factors are crossed when every relevant level of one appears with every relevant level of the other.
A lower-level factor is nested when each of its levels occurs within only one parent-factor level.
The decisive distinction is whether the same lower-level identities recur across parent levels or are unique within a parent.
major_error_concepts: Estimating a lab by annotator interaction as though every annotator served every lab.

cards.prompt: Define Effect hierarchy and heredity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The modeling principles that lower-order terms and parents of active interactions deserve protection while remaining scientific assumptions not design facts.
required_concepts: The modeling principles that lower-order terms and parents of active interactions deserve protection while remaining scientific assumptions not design facts.
major_error_concepts: Deleting a main effect solely by p-value while keeping its interaction.

cards.prompt: Define Effect-versus-coefficient scaling. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The convention that a two-level effect is often twice the corresponding coefficient under -1/+1 regression coding.
required_concepts: The convention that a two-level effect is often twice the corresponding coefficient under -1/+1 regression coding.
major_error_concepts: Reporting 3 without naming whether it is a coefficient or effect.

cards.prompt: Define Factor and level. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A controlled input dimension and one of its prespecified settings within the design region.
required_concepts: A controlled input dimension and one of its prespecified settings within the design region.
major_error_concepts: Calling response categories factor levels.

cards.prompt: Define Factorial contrast column. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A plus-minus product column whose signed response sum estimates a declared main or interaction contrast after scaling.
required_concepts: A plus-minus product column whose signed response sum estimates a declared main or interaction contrast after scaling.
major_error_concepts: Adding factor codes instead of multiplying for interaction.

cards.prompt: Define Factorial design matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The row-complete matrix of intercept factor interaction and optional block columns tied to actual treatment combinations.
required_concepts: The row-complete matrix of intercept factor interaction and optional block columns tied to actual treatment combinations.
major_error_concepts: Using a matrix whose rows do not match assignment records.

cards.prompt: Define Full factorial design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A design including every treatment combination of the declared factor levels so main and interaction contrasts are available within the region.
required_concepts: A design including every treatment combination of the declared factor levels so main and interaction contrasts are available within the region.
major_error_concepts: Calling a sparse subset full factorial.

cards.prompt: Define Interaction and effect plots. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** graphical displays of cell means or effects used to expose patterns while estimates and uncertainty remain tied to the design.
required_concepts: graphical displays of cell means or effects used to expose patterns while estimates and uncertainty remain tied to the design.
major_error_concepts: Using plot appearance without replication or scale qualification as a test.

cards.prompt: Define Interaction effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The difference in one factor's effect across levels of another factor revealing nonadditivity on the response scale.
required_concepts: The difference in one factor's effect across levels of another factor revealing nonadditivity on the response scale.
major_error_concepts: Calling crossing plot lines merely visual noise without a contrast.

cards.prompt: Define Main effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared average change across levels of one factor averaged over a specified distribution or equal weighting of other-factor levels.
required_concepts: The declared average change across levels of one factor averaged over a specified distribution or equal weighting of other-factor levels.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting the average as universal when interaction is large or weighting differs in the target.

cards.prompt: Define Minus-plus effect coding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The frozen use of -1 and +1 for two-level factors so contrast columns and regression coefficients have declared scaling.
required_concepts: The frozen use of -1 and +1 for two-level factors so contrast columns and regression coefficients have declared scaling.
major_error_concepts: Switching row order without recomputing signs.

cards.prompt: Define One-factor-at-a-time failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The design path changing one factor from a baseline while holding others fixed which cannot identify general interactions and covers fewer joint settings.
required_concepts: The design path changing one factor from a baseline while holding others fixed which cannot identify general interactions and covers fewer joint settings.
major_error_concepts: Claiming separate positive changes prove their combination is additive.

cards.term: Pure error versus lack of fit
cards.prompt: Define Pure error versus lack of fit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** variation among true replicates at the same treatment combination separated from model lack of fit and owned analytically downstream.
required_concepts: variation among true replicates at the same treatment combination separated from model lack of fit and owned analytically downstream.
major_error_concepts: Calling any regression residual pure error when cells are unreplicated.

cards.prompt: Define Simple effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The effect of one factor at a fixed level of another factor.
required_concepts: The effect of one factor at a fixed level of another factor.
major_error_concepts: Calling one simple effect the overall main effect.

cards.prompt: Define Treatment combination and cell. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** one joint setting containing one level from every crossed factor and the experimental units assigned to it.
required_concepts: one joint setting containing one level from every crossed factor and the experimental units assigned to it.
major_error_concepts: Adding levels to get five cells.

cards.prompt: Using four means mu_ab with a,b in {-1,+1}, reconstruct both main effects and the interaction, declaring the effect/coefficient scaling convention.
cards.definition: Let m_pp,m_pm,m_mp,m_mm denote the means at (A,B)=(+1,+1),(+1,-1),(-1,+1),(-1,-1). The simple A effects are d_plus=m_pp-m_mp and d_minus=m_pm-m_mm. The equal-weight A main effect is (d_plus+d_minus)/2; the B main effect is [(m_pp-m_pm)+(m_mp-m_mm)]/2. The difference-in-differences interaction is d_plus-d_minus. Under the usual two-level factorial-effect convention the AB effect is half this interaction, and under ±1 regression coding beta_AB is one quarter of it. A declared consistent convention is essential.
required_concepts: Recover both main effects by averaging the relevant two simple contrasts.
Calculate the difference between simple A effects to expose interaction.
Distinguish difference-in-differences, the usual factorial AB effect, and the ±1 regression coefficient.
major_error_concepts: The difference-in-differences interaction, the two-level factorial AB effect, and beta_AB are always numerically equal.

cards.prompt: Define Alias set. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The effects sharing identical or sign-reversed columns in the selected fraction and therefore not separately estimable from that data alone.
required_concepts: The effects sharing identical or sign-reversed columns in the selected fraction and therefore not separately estimable from that data alone.
major_error_concepts: Labeling the A estimate as pure when BC may be active.

cards.prompt: Define Center-point curvature test. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The comparison of replicated center responses with the factorial corner mean to detect aggregate departure from a first-order plane.
required_concepts: The comparison of replicated center responses with the factorial corner mean to detect aggregate departure from a first-order plane.
major_error_concepts: Selecting an optimum from one center point.

cards.prompt: Define Central-composite-design boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The augmentation of factorial or fractional points with axial and center points to estimate a local quadratic surface under design-region and replication requirements.
required_concepts: A central composite design augments factorial or fractional points with axial points.
It also includes center points to estimate a local quadratic surface under design-region and replication requirements.
major_error_concepts: Calling any quadratic regression a response-surface design.

cards.prompt: Define Defining relation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The set of words equal to the identity column obtained from generators and their products.
required_concepts: The set of words equal to the identity column obtained from generators and their products.
major_error_concepts: Treating the generator equation and defining word as unrelated conventions.

cards.prompt: Define Effect sparsity assumption. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The scientific expectation that only a small subset of many candidate effects is practically active and thus supports screening interpretation.
required_concepts: The scientific expectation that only a small subset of many candidate effects is practically active and thus supports screening interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Treating sparsity as a theorem supplied by the design.

cards.prompt: Define Factorial blocking generator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A deliberate confounding of selected treatment interactions with block contrasts to run a factorial under resource batches.
required_concepts: A deliberate confounding of selected treatment interactions with block contrasts to run a factorial under resource batches.
major_error_concepts: Choosing a block generator after observing effects.

cards.prompt: Define First-order response-surface model. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The local linear model used after screening to estimate a direction of improvement inside a specified region without global claims.
required_concepts: The local linear model used after screening to estimate a direction of improvement inside a specified region without global claims.
major_error_concepts: Extrapolating the linear surface indefinitely.

cards.prompt: Define Foldover design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A complementary follow-up fraction chosen to break selected alias relationships when combined with the original runs.
required_concepts: A complementary follow-up fraction chosen to break selected alias relationships when combined with the original runs.
major_error_concepts: Claiming one foldover resolves every possible higher-order alias.

cards.prompt: Define Fraction generator. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An equation assigning one factor column as a product of others to select the fraction.
required_concepts: An equation assigning one factor column as a product of others to select the fraction.
major_error_concepts: Writing a generator but building rows that violate it.

cards.prompt: Define Fractional-screening hierarchy and heredity assumptions. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The expectations that lower-order effects dominate and active interactions often involve active parent factors used specifically to prioritize de-aliasing and follow-up in a fraction.
required_concepts: The hierarchy assumption expects lower-order effects to dominate.
The heredity assumption expects active interactions to involve active parent factors; both assumptions guide de-aliasing and follow-up rather than prove inactivity.
major_error_concepts: Forcing every scientific system to obey strong heredity or using heredity as proof that an alias is inactive.

cards.prompt: Define Partial confounding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** changing which treatment effect is confounded with blocks across replicated factorials so information can be recovered across replicates.
required_concepts: changing which treatment effect is confounded with blocks across replicated factorials so information can be recovered across replicates.
major_error_concepts: Calling the design unconfounded within each replicate.

cards.prompt: What is the screening role of Plackett-Burman designs, and when does regular-fraction alias algebra fail?
cards.definition: Plackett-Burman screening designs use balanced, pairwise-orthogonal two-level main-effect columns to screen many factors economically. Common non-power-of-two designs such as 12 or 20 runs are nonregular and partially alias main effects with interactions; their interpretation cannot simply reuse regular defining-word algebra. Power-of-two members can coincide with regular fractional factorials, so regularity must be checked for the actual design.
required_concepts: The design is for economical main-effect screening using orthogonal main-effect columns.
Typical non-power-of-two members have partial interaction aliasing.
Do not declare every member nonregular or infer that interactions are absent.
major_error_concepts: Every Plackett-Burman design has unaliased interactions because its main-effect columns are orthogonal.

cards.prompt: Define Regular fractional factorial. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A systematically selected `2^(k-p)` subset defined by p independent generators with algebraic alias structure.
required_concepts: A systematically selected `2^(k-p)` subset defined by p independent generators with algebraic alias structure.
major_error_concepts: Calling any eight of 32 combinations a regular quarter fraction.

cards.prompt: Define Resolution III design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A defining relation whose shortest nonidentity word has length three so main effects can alias two-factor interactions.
required_concepts: A defining relation whose shortest nonidentity word has length three so main effects can alias two-factor interactions.
major_error_concepts: Claiming main effects are clear because no two main effects alias each other.

cards.prompt: Define resolution exactly IV for a regular two-level fractional factorial and state its aliasing consequences.
cards.definition: For a regular two-level fractional factorial, resolution exactly IV means the shortest nonidentity word in its defining relation has length four. Thus main effects are unaliased with other main effects and two-factor interactions, while two-factor interactions can alias other two-factor interactions. Higher-resolution designs also satisfy some of these clear-main-effect properties; the minimum word length distinguishes exact resolution.
required_concepts: Declare a regular two-level fraction and minimum nonidentity word length four.
Main effects are clear of two-factor interactions.
Two-factor interactions need not be clear of each other.
major_error_concepts: Every design whose main effects are clear of two-factor interactions has resolution exactly IV.

cards.prompt: Define resolution exactly V for a regular two-level fractional factorial and state its aliasing consequences.
cards.definition: For a regular two-level fractional factorial, resolution exactly V means the shortest nonidentity defining word has length five. Main effects are clear of interactions through order three, and two-factor interactions are clear of one another but may alias three-factor interactions. This does not assert that the aliased higher-order effects are zero.
required_concepts: Minimum nonidentity defining-word length is five in a regular two-level fraction.
Main effects are clear through order three.
Two-factor interactions are mutually clear but can alias three-factor interactions.
major_error_concepts: Resolution V guarantees that every three-factor interaction vanishes.

cards.prompt: Define Screening design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An economical early-stage design intended to identify promising factors or alias groups rather than certify a final optimum or mechanism.
required_concepts: An economical early-stage design intended to identify promising factors or alias groups rather than certify a final optimum or mechanism.
major_error_concepts: Reporting a screened main effect as a confirmed isolated mechanism.

cards.prompt: Define Steepest-ascent path. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The sequence of experimental settings along the fitted first-order gradient with step sizes and stopping checks declared.
required_concepts: The sequence of experimental settings along the fitted first-order gradient with step sizes and stopping checks declared.
major_error_concepts: Jumping directly beyond the design region and calling the predicted point optimal.

cards.prompt: Define Cluster design effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The equal-size approximation `1+(m-1)rho` inflating variance or required iid-equivalent sample size for cluster size m and ICC rho.
required_concepts: The equal-size approximation `1+(m-1)rho` inflating variance or required iid-equivalent sample size for cluster size m and ICC rho.
major_error_concepts: Using rho itself as the sample-size multiplier.

cards.prompt: Define Cluster randomization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** assignment of intact groups when treatment delivery contamination or logistics operate at group level.
required_concepts: assignment of intact groups when treatment delivery contamination or logistics operate at group level.
major_error_concepts: Analyzing employees as independently assigned.

cards.prompt: Define Contamination. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** control units receiving aspects of treatment or treatment units receiving control which changes exposure contrasts and may motivate cluster assignment.
required_concepts: control units receiving aspects of treatment or treatment units receiving control which changes exposure contrasts and may motivate cluster assignment.
major_error_concepts: Dropping contaminated units after outcome inspection.

cards.prompt: Define Effective sample-size diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The rough iid-equivalent information `N/design_effect` used for intuition rather than a replacement for design-specific power.
required_concepts: The rough iid-equivalent information `N/design_effect` used for intuition rather than a replacement for design-specific power.
major_error_concepts: Reporting 200 as the exact number of independent clusters or degrees of freedom.

cards.prompt: Define Exposure mapping. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A prespecified function reducing the full assignment vector to treatment and spillover conditions relevant for each unit.
required_concepts: A prespecified function reducing the full assignment vector to treatment and spillover conditions relevant for each unit.
major_error_concepts: Inventing exposure groups after viewing network outcomes.

cards.prompt: Define Hard-to-change factor. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: A hard-to-change factor is one whose level is costly, slow, or operationally difficult to reset for each small experimental unit. This can motivate assigning its levels to batches or whole plots instead. An oven temperature held for a batch is an example; the difficulty does not justify pretending it was independently randomized for every specimen.
required_concepts: Changing the factor level for each small unit is operationally difficult or costly, motivating a restricted assignment level.
The analysis must respect the actual assignment level rather than inventing independent resets.
accepted_variants: Oven temperature may be reset between batches rather than between specimens because resetting is slow. Specimens within one temperature batch are not independently randomized temperature replications.
major_error_concepts: Treating every specimen in one oven batch as if oven temperature had been separately randomized for it.

cards.prompt: Define Interference and SUTVA boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The condition that one unit's potential outcome may depend on other units' assignments so the ordinary two-potential-outcome representation is incomplete.
required_concepts: The condition that one unit's potential outcome may depend on other units' assignments so the ordinary two-potential-outcome representation is incomplete.
major_error_concepts: Using a simple user ATE without describing shared exposure.

cards.prompt: Define Intracluster correlation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The correlation of outcomes among observations in the same cluster that reduces independent information relative to equal iid rows.
required_concepts: The correlation of outcomes among observations in the same cluster that reduces independent information relative to equal iid rows.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a small ICC is irrelevant when clusters are large.

cards.prompt: Define Minimum detectable effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The effect magnitude achieving the specified target power for a fixed sample and design rather than the smallest scientifically meaningful effect.
required_concepts: The effect magnitude achieving the specified target power for a fixed sample and design rather than the smallest scientifically meaningful effect.
major_error_concepts: Calling MDE the true expected effect or a significance threshold on the estimate.

cards.prompt: Define Nested factor. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A factor whose levels are unique within levels of another factor and therefore do not form a full cross.
required_concepts: A factor whose levels are unique within levels of another factor and therefore do not form a full cross.
major_error_concepts: Estimating model by run interaction from a nested structure.

cards.prompt: Define Prospective power inputs. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The complete pre-outcome set of target effect variance alpha power allocation dependence attrition multiplicity horizon and estimator assumptions.
required_concepts: The complete pre-outcome set of target effect variance alpha power allocation dependence attrition multiplicity horizon and estimator assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Reporting power without the assumed effect or dependence.

cards.prompt: Define Random-factor boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A factor whose observed levels are treated as sampled from a wider population for variance-component or generalization purposes with a declared sampling story.
required_concepts: A factor whose observed levels are treated as sampled from a wider population for variance-component or generalization purposes with a declared sampling story.
major_error_concepts: Calling any inconvenient factor random to avoid estimating its levels.

cards.prompt: Define Randomization-analysis unit alignment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The requirement that uncertainty and reference distributions preserve the level and restrictions of assignment even when responses are lower-level.
required_concepts: The requirement that uncertainty and reference distributions preserve the level and restrictions of assignment even when responses are lower-level.
major_error_concepts: Permuting users across treatment arms.

cards.prompt: Define Repeated-measures dependence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** multiple outcomes on one unit across time conditions or trials whose correlation and order must be represented.
required_concepts: multiple outcomes on one unit across time conditions or trials whose correlation and order must be represented.
major_error_concepts: Powering and testing by day rows as iid.

cards.prompt: Define Split-plot assignment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The two-stage randomization of whole-plot factor levels to whole plots and subplot factor levels within each whole plot.
required_concepts: The two-stage randomization of whole-plot factor levels to whole plots and subplot factor levels within each whole plot.
major_error_concepts: Randomly permuting treatments across all small plots as if whole-plot restrictions and the within-whole-plot assignment stage did not exist.

cards.prompt: Define Split-plot error strata. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinct variation sources supporting whole-plot and subplot effects because factors were randomized at different levels.
required_concepts: The distinct variation sources supporting whole-plot and subplot effects because factors were randomized at different levels.
major_error_concepts: Testing the whole-plot factor against the subplot error term.

cards.prompt: Define Unequal cluster sizes. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The loss and weighting complications when cluster membership varies which make the equal-size design-effect formula only approximate.
required_concepts: The loss and weighting complications when cluster membership varies which make the equal-size design-effect formula only approximate.
major_error_concepts: Substituting average size and ignoring size variation or informative size.

cards.prompt: Define Whole plot and subplot. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: In a split-plot design, a whole plot is the experimental unit assigned the whole-plot factor; its nested subplots are the experimental units assigned the subplot factor. Hard-to-change settings often motivate whole-plot assignment, but relative difficulty is not the defining requirement. Several subplots within one irrigation-assigned whole plot do not provide several independent irrigation-assignment replications; inference must respect the relevant assignment level and dependence.
required_concepts: Distinguish whole-plot assignment units from the subplot assignment units nested within them.
Subplots sharing one whole-plot assignment are not separate independent replications of that assignment.
major_error_concepts: Treating every subplot within one irrigation-assigned whole plot as an independent irrigation-assignment replicate.

cards.prompt: Define A/A experiment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** assignment of nominally identical experiences used to validate randomization logging metrics and false-positive calibration end to end.
required_concepts: assignment of nominally identical experiences used to validate randomization logging metrics and false-positive calibration end to end.
major_error_concepts: Demanding every A/A p-value exceed 0.05 or treating one pass as permanent platform proof.

cards.prompt: Define Alpha-spending boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A function allocating cumulative Type I error over information time so unplanned calendar timing can be accommodated within the declared design.
required_concepts: A function allocating cumulative Type I error over information time so unplanned calendar timing can be accommodated within the declared design.
major_error_concepts: Treating alpha as a budget that can be restored after a nonsignificant look.

cards.prompt: Define Always-valid inference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A sequential procedure whose p-values confidence sequences or evidence process retain their stated guarantee at permitted stopping times under exact assumptions.
required_concepts: An always-valid procedure produces p-values, confidence sequences, or an evidence process for sequential use.
The stated guarantee holds at permitted stopping times under the procedure's exact assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Calling any repeatedly displayed confidence interval a confidence sequence.

cards.prompt: Define Exposure and persistence integrity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** verification that assigned units consistently received only their intended variant and cross-device cache retry or routing behavior did not mix arms.
required_concepts: verification that assigned units consistently received only their intended variant and cross-device cache retry or routing behavior did not mix arms.
major_error_concepts: Analyzing by session label as though assignments were independent.

cards.prompt: Define Fixed-horizon design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A protocol with predetermined sample size or information time and one planned terminal analysis under its stated error guarantee.
required_concepts: A protocol with predetermined sample size or information time and one planned terminal analysis under its stated error guarantee.
major_error_concepts: Stopping early for significance while reporting the original fixed-horizon p-value.

cards.prompt: Define Futility rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A prespecified stopping criterion for insufficient promise that can save resources while its binding status and operating effects are declared.
required_concepts: A prespecified stopping criterion for insufficient promise that can save resources while its binding status and operating effects are declared.
major_error_concepts: Adding a futility stop only after an inconvenient trend appears.

cards.prompt: Define Group-sequential design. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A finite set of planned interim analyses with joint boundaries calibrated to control overall error and support early efficacy or futility decisions.
required_concepts: A finite set of planned interim analyses with joint boundaries calibrated to control overall error and support early efficacy or futility decisions.
major_error_concepts: Using nominal fixed-test cutoffs at all looks.

cards.prompt: Define Interim look. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A prespecified analysis before the final horizon whose frequency statistic boundary and permitted decisions belong to the design.
required_concepts: A prespecified analysis before the final horizon whose frequency statistic boundary and permitted decisions belong to the design.
major_error_concepts: Calling dashboard refreshes informal when decisions are influenced by them.

cards.prompt: Define Logging loss and differential missingness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integrity problem where outcomes or eligibility records are absent and loss may depend on treatment or outcome.
required_concepts: The integrity problem where outcomes or eligibility records are absent and loss may depend on treatment or outcome.
major_error_concepts: Assuming missing logs are equally distributed without evidence.

cards.prompt: Define Multiplicity family. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared collection of hypotheses or decisions sharing an error guarantee rather than every number on a dashboard.
required_concepts: The declared collection of hypotheses or decisions sharing an error guarantee rather than every number on a dashboard.
major_error_concepts: Treating each metric's 0.05 test as a five-percent family decision.

cards.prompt: Why can applying fixed-sample thresholds under naive optional stopping invalidate nominal error control?
cards.definition: Naive optional stopping repeatedly applies a fixed-sample threshold and stops when it is crossed, while reporting the original fixed-sample calibration. Its overall Type I error can exceed the nominal level because the rejection event is a union over looks. Inflation is not strict for every possible dependence pattern; a valid sequential or anytime procedure must control the whole stopping rule.
required_concepts: The stopping decision uses repeated fixed-sample rejections.
Single-look calibration does not generally control the union over looks.
A declared sequential guarantee is different from assuming every look is separately valid.
major_error_concepts: Since each individual look has a five-percent rejection probability, any number of adaptively chosen looks also has exactly five-percent overall error.

cards.prompt: Define Novelty and carryover checks. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** time-pattern diagnostics for transient adoption effects lingering exposure or treatment decay that qualify horizon and generalization claims.
required_concepts: time-pattern diagnostics for transient adoption effects lingering exposure or treatment decay that qualify horizon and generalization claims.
major_error_concepts: Averaging away the pattern and claiming persistent benefit.

cards.prompt: Define Outcome switching. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** changing the primary response direction time window subgroup or transform after observing data which invalidates the original confirmatory calibration.
required_concepts: changing the primary response direction time window subgroup or transform after observing data which invalidates the original confirmatory calibration.
major_error_concepts: Replacing the primary metric in the report without a deviation record.

cards.prompt: Define Prespecified pretreatment covariate adjustment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** variance reduction using information measured before assignment with method and variable definitions frozen before outcome inspection.
required_concepts: variance reduction using information measured before assignment with method and variable definitions frozen before outcome inspection.
major_error_concepts: Using post-treatment activity as a baseline covariate.

cards.term: Primary secondary guardrail and diagnostic roles
cards.prompt: Define Primary secondary guardrail and diagnostic roles. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The noninterchangeable outcome roles that determine decision priority error control and interpretation.
required_concepts: The noninterchangeable outcome roles that determine decision priority error control and interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Promoting whichever role looks favorable after results.

cards.prompt: Define Safety stopping rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A prespecified rapid-action boundary for harm or operational failure kept distinct from the primary efficacy error claim.
required_concepts: A prespecified rapid-action boundary for harm or operational failure kept distinct from the primary efficacy error claim.
major_error_concepts: Continuing because the primary metric looks favorable.

cards.prompt: Define Sample-ratio mismatch. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A statistically implausible difference between observed and configured assignment counts that signals routing eligibility logging exposure or data-loss defects.
required_concepts: A statistically implausible difference between observed and configured assignment counts that signals routing eligibility logging exposure or data-loss defects.
major_error_concepts: Adjusting estimates for arm size and ignoring why allocation failed.

cards.prompt: Define Analysis-ready experimental-design record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The design matrix contrasts unit structure randomization reference set weights covariance needs exclusions and deviations supplied to statistical analysis.
required_concepts: The design matrix contrasts unit structure randomization reference set weights covariance needs exclusions and deviations supplied to statistical analysis.
major_error_concepts: Handing over a flat CSV with no assignment metadata.

cards.prompt: Define Causal-identification boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The interface from randomized assignment foundations to observational noncompliance mediation instruments and other identification problems.
required_concepts: The interface from randomized assignment foundations to observational noncompliance mediation instruments and other identification problems.
major_error_concepts: Applying experimental vocabulary to an observational regression.

cards.prompt: Define Design-stage property evidence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Evidence established before outcomes, analytically or by simulation, for a prespecified operating characteristic of a design, such as assignment balance, alias resolution, power, or sequential validity; it is not evidence of an empirical treatment effect.
required_concepts: The evidence concerns a prespecified design operating characteristic and is established analytically or by simulation before outcomes are observed.
A design-stage property such as balance, alias resolution, power, or sequential validity is not evidence of an empirical treatment effect.
major_error_concepts: Upgrading a design property to an empirical effect conclusion.

cards.prompt: Define Estimand-to-analysis mapping. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit correspondence among target effect assignment mechanism observed variables estimator weights uncertainty method and missingness handling.
required_concepts: The explicit correspondence among target effect assignment mechanism observed variables estimator weights uncertainty method and missingness handling.
major_error_concepts: Choosing an estimator because it gives the desired sign.

cards.prompt: Define Execution-integrity evidence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The A/A SRM exposure fidelity logging missingness attrition version and contamination checks needed before ordinary effect interpretation.
required_concepts: The A/A SRM exposure fidelity logging missingness attrition version and contamination checks needed before ordinary effect interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Treating diagnostics as optional because randomization code passed a unit test.

cards.prompt: Define External-validity boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The separate argument required to transport an internally valid result across populations settings times treatments or measurement systems.
required_concepts: The separate argument required to transport an internally valid result across populations settings times treatments or measurement systems.
major_error_concepts: Treating randomization as a guarantee of representativeness.

cards.prompt: Define Independent confirmation run. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A fresh prespecified experiment testing an exploratory selection or repaired design on new eligible units without reusing selection outcomes as confirmation.
required_concepts: A fresh prespecified experiment testing an exploratory selection or repaired design on new eligible units without reusing selection outcomes as confirmation.
major_error_concepts: Calling the best screened cell independently confirmed by the same data.

cards.prompt: Define Internal-validity conclusion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The narrow causal or comparative conclusion supported for the assigned units under execution and analysis assumptions.
required_concepts: The narrow causal or comparative conclusion supported for the assigned units under execution and analysis assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Generalizing automatically to users domains or future model versions.

cards.prompt: Define Protocol identity package. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned question eligibility treatment control outcome unit assignment horizon analysis decision source and approval record that defines the experiment.
required_concepts: The versioned question eligibility treatment control outcome unit assignment horizon analysis decision source and approval record that defines the experiment.
major_error_concepts: Using a title alone while implementation changes.

cards.prompt: Why does a randomized comparison not, by itself, establish that its outcome measures the intended construct?
cards.definition: Random assignment supports comparison of assigned treatments on the recorded outcome under the design's assumptions. It does not establish that the outcome adequately represents the intended construct. A randomized teaching study using a timed reading score can estimate an effect on that score without thereby validating it as a measure of every aspect of comprehension. Measurement validity needs its own evidence; randomization and valid measurement answer different questions.
required_concepts: Randomization concerns treatment comparisons on the specified measured outcome, subject to design assumptions.
Construct validity concerns whether that outcome represents the intended concept; randomization alone cannot establish it.
accepted_variants: Randomizing classrooms can support a causal comparison of their recorded test scores. Whether the test measures the intended learning construct remains a separate measurement question, so a clean randomized difference does not validate the instrument by itself.
major_error_concepts: Claiming that random treatment assignment automatically makes any chosen score a valid and comprehensive measure of the intended construct.

cards.prompt: Define Replication and reproducibility package. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between repeating computation reproducing the recorded result and independently replicating the scientific comparison under a new assignment.
required_concepts: The distinction between repeating computation reproducing the recorded result and independently replicating the scientific comparison under a new assignment.
major_error_concepts: Calling deterministic rerun evidence of generality.

cards.prompt: Define Statistical evidence versus deployment authorization. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The independent policy and technical gates not supplied by statistical power randomization or a positive effect.
required_concepts: The independent policy and technical gates not supplied by statistical power randomization or a positive effect.
major_error_concepts: Using net average benefit as blanket safety authorization.

description: A definition-recall course deck covering core concepts in Experimental Design.
